hints: Look closely at the three lines around 0.2 s. The solid line shoots sharply upwards at W and then crosses the dashed line at X. Think about which chamber is contracting to cause that sharp rise.

Remember the golden rule for valves: a valve opens when pressure behind it becomes higher than pressure in front of it, and closes when pressure in front becomes higher. Apply this first at W and X, then at Y and Z around 0.45 s.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three pressure lines**

First, let's make friends with the graph. The dotted low line is atrial pressure, the solid line that rises and falls sharply is ventricular pressure, and the dashed high line is arterial pressure in the aorta.

At about 0.15 to 0.2 s the ventricle starts to contract, so ventricular pressure (solid) rises very fast.

**Work out W and X at the start of ventricular systole**

At W, ventricular pressure just rises above atrial pressure. Blood would try to flow back into the atrium, so the atrioventricular valves slam shut. This causes the first heart sound.

A moment later at X, ventricular pressure rises above arterial pressure in the aorta. Now blood can push forward, so the semi-lunar valves open and blood is ejected.

**Work out Y and Z at the end of ventricular systole**

Around 0.45 s the ventricle relaxes, so ventricular pressure (solid) falls fast. At Y, ventricular pressure falls below arterial pressure. Blood tries to flow back into the ventricle, so the semi-lunar valves close. Notice the little notch or dip in the aortic pressure line.

Then at Z, ventricular pressure falls even further below atrial pressure. Blood can now flow from atrium to ventricle again, so the atrioventricular valves open. That gives the sequence: AV close, SL open, SL close, AV open.

options.A: W is correct as AV valves close, but X and Y are swapped. X is when ventricular pressure exceeds arterial pressure so SL valves open, not close.
options.B: Perfect sequence. W is AV close, X is SL open for ejection, Y is SL close as ventricle relaxes, and Z is AV open for ventricular filling.
options.C: Starts with the wrong valves. W is caused by ventricular contraction pushing against the atrium, so it is AV close, not SL close.
options.D: Reverses the whole logic. W cannot be SL open because ventricular pressure is still lower than arterial pressure at W, and Z cannot be SL close because that event already happened at Y.
